title: Implement request-debounce shim to stop repeat-retry waves
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During a customer escalation on 2026-02-18 a small subset of high-throughput tenants experienced repeat 5xx waves and cascading timeouts. Root cause analysis shows an interaction between long-lived streaming requests, client SDK aggressive retry heuristics, and a transient queue starvation condition in the front proxy when connection reuse faltered. Instead of immediately addressing all long-tail causes (TLS session churn, kernel scheduling), this ticket implements a short-term server-side 'request-debounce' shim to prevent immediate identical-request retries from amplifying failures while we complete longer-term fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Debounce shim deployed in edge proxy and runtime: identical request fingerprints within 250ms are short-circuited to a single upstream execution with a stable idempotency token
Incidents similar to 2026-02-18 do not cause >0.1% 5xx for affected tenants during a controlled traffic surge test (50x baseline)
New telemetry events available in Console: debounce.hit, debounce.bypass, debounce.queue_depth, per-tenant debounce rate
Automated canary rollout across regions with rollback signal tied to error-rate and latency regression thresholds
steps_taken: 2026-02-18 10:12 — Incident triage: incoming reports from three customers showed high 5xx rates and duplicate request traces clustered within 200-400ms windows
2026-02-18 12:04 — Live mitigation: increased circuit-breaker aggressiveness for impacted tenants and temporarily routed heavy tenants to lower-concurrency pools (manual operator action)
2026-02-19 — RCA: traced amplification to SDK-level hedging + client replays when TCP keepalive failed; proxy queued repeated identical payloads which saturated runtime shard queues

2026-02-20 — Spike test in staging reproduces repeat-retry amplification; designed debounce prototype (server-side idempotency dedupe for N ms) and local benchmark shows 30-60% reduction in peak inflight requests under replay patterns
2026-02-22 — Implemented debounce prototype in edge-proxy (feature flag) and wired minimal telemetry events; smoke-tested against synthetic replay generator
2026-02-24 — Internal review: prototype approved pending safety guard and canary plan. Created this ticket to track production rollout, automation, and complementary follow-ups
decisions: Short-term: introduce server-side debounce (250ms default) to collapse rapid identical requests into single upstream execution rather than returning immediate 5xxs or allowing duplicates to queue
Safety guard: debounce must never delay first request; it only collapses near-duplicate subsequent requests and returns the upstream result to waiters
Telemetry-first rollout: expose debounce metrics and a per-tenant kill-switch before broad rollout
Long-term: continue parallel work on connection keepalive robustness, SDK retry guidance, and per-tenant backlog quotas (tracked in separate tickets)
review_notes: PM (Samira Cho): ensure messaging clarifies this is a mitigation, not a root-cause fix; include expected impact window
Security (Liam O'Connor): debounce introduces short-lived in-memory idempotency keys; verified no PII retention and keys rotate per-request lifecycle
Infra (Jae Park): flagged that debounce must be localized to proxy instance to avoid cross-node coordination; approved with per-node memory cap
QA (Maya Patel): request fingerprinting must be robust to benign reordering (headers vs body canonicalization); added unit tests

Follow-up: add automated rollback if debounce causes latency p99 regressions >25ms or user-visible error-rate >0.05%
